title: Document REPOLib
body:
I wrote a little bit of documentation, and set `<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>`.

I would also advice to search all these comments: `// TODO: Document this.` and document those files.

Also feel free to check that the documentation is accurate.
author: Hamunii

comments.body:
Maybe this is a hot take, but I feel like a lot of these (and a lot of C# XML docs in general) are redundant, as the definition of the thing is self-explanatory. For example the `<param>` tags and those that describe classes like `DictionaryExtensions`. In my opinion these only bloat the source and make it harder to read (something C# already struggles with). 

I feel like the compiler warnings only make this worse, basically forcing you to annotate everything. I'm not sure if there's a way to turn those off, but I would much prefer that over adding even more bloat in the form of `#pragma` lines.

Some docs definitely are redundant, but having docs there when you need them is nice. And yes docs do bloat the source code, but there's nothing that can be done about it. Also as the person who wrote the code, it's obvious what the code does without documentation. But to someone who didn't write the code, it might not be clear at all.

I also think the compiler warnings are great so you are indeed forced to annotate everything that is a part of the public API. It also makes you think more about if some thing should be a part of the public API or not. This is just what maintaining an API is about, you are creating something for other people to use and not necessarily yourself.

Simply put, if you are making an API which does not have xml docs, it's worse than if the API had xml docs. I'd get your argument if this was not an API, but this is an API.

> I do see your perspective, but I definitely value brevity and ease of understanding more than completeness for completeness sake. I simply think there's a better balance we can strive for. For example, I can't think of a case when stuff like this would be useful for the user:

I do agree that this example in particular is where the docs aren't really needed, but even here, it can make things slightly more clear to users, which is what we care about as an API. And at the very least it doesn't hurt to have it (from the users' perspective). It's also not a big deal to write documentation for things that are fairly obvious or easy to figure out.

> On another note, I definitely think REPOLib could reconsider which parts are public API and not, but I don't think this is the best way to do that.

I do agree with that, but also thinking about what should and should not be a part of the public API is only a side effect of having to write documentation for public members.

comments.body: I notice you removed the try catch wrapper for the `type.GetMethods()` line, so it might result in the `TypeLoadException: Could not resolve the signature of a virtual method` error, though I don't know if `HarmonyLib.AccessTools.GetTypesFromAssembly` will prevent the type from loading which had that method. I guess it just needs to be tested.

That was a misunderstanding on my part. I've made the appropriate changes now.

I've done a bit of research into the exception and just about everywhere I look I get a different answer. 
* .NET version difference/compatibility
* Issues with running under proton
* It just magically went away??
* dotnet [Emit] bug (Generation of metadata for reflection)
* Updating something fixed it (OS, Unity, etc.)
* Missing or unloaded assemblies

So as unfortunate as it may be, the quickest solution is likely a try/catch block. 

As for `HarmonyLib.AccessTools.GetTypesFromAssembly`...
I am doubtful that the provided function will resolve this issue however, as you suggested its another safety net that should be added before its needed so I've included it in here as apart of my 2 for 1 special 😄

title: NetworkedEvent system (using PhotonNetwork.RaiseEvent) and example patch
body:
Hey Zehs,

We talked briefly about potential ``PhotonNetwork.RaiseEvent`` usage. I originally made this system for my own mod but I think it would definitely be better suited for a centralized library so I ported my code over

Unfortunately one **MAJOR** drawback I don't think I can account for is that Photon's RaiseEvent must be associated with a unique byte from _1-200_

This is the main issue I forsee with this system.

If any other mods or the basegame decided to create and subscribe to an event it is next to impossible to determine what number they used. Luckily it doesn't appear that the REPO developers have used this system for custom network events. Also I think most average mod devs will stick to standard Rpcs for the most part (when it comes to networking). 

Otherwise, this system allows for simple networking events without having to register a network prefab or assign it to a particular object. You are limited only by what you can accomplish with a serialized object. In my mod's particular case, this allows me to invoke an enumerator on all clients from a local client patch.

I also provided a rough example in REPOLib where I patched RoomVolumeCheck.CheckSet to detect when a player has arrived at the ship. It's a very rough patch and is mostly there to show the different network event usage. I also cannot verify that RaiseOthers does work as intended, however I'm pretty certain it does from the PUN documentation. Personally i'd recommend commenting it out before publishing any changes to thunderstore. I just left it as-is so you could check it out
